space: game axes: x left, y up, z forward, metres; yaw in radians about +y; fov = vertical degrees (three.js)

camera_spaces.vehicle: local to the root of the asset named in relative_to (the player's vehicle unless stated)
camera_spaces.asset: local to the stamped asset named in relative_to
camera_spaces.layout: the space of public/world/layouts/<relative_to>.json — add the offset and yaw the chapter stamps that layout with
camera_spaces.set: local to this transition's own set (see set.anchor)

order.change: was order 4; now reads as the departure toward Chile

stage_tense.note: Which stages are memories and which are plans is the owner's to state; the director only reserves the visual treatment.
stage_tense.japan: future / aspiration per the owner's brief — never caption it as something that happened. Treatment: the t03 route line is dashed over the jump, and the stage opens in first light.
stage_tense.others: to be confirmed in the narrative review before any caption uses the past tense

grammar.letterbox: use the engine's existing cine bars (emit('cine', true)) for the whole of every transition; input locked (st.lock)
grammar.one_idea: each transition is one shape handed from one vehicle to the next: circle, doorway, horizon, light, white
grammar.camera: one continuous move per side, eased in and out (sine); never more than 2 m/s of camera travel near people, never a roll; hold at least 1 s on the matched frame before and after a splice
grammar.splice: always on a frame the engine can hold as a still (held-frame overlay) — that still is the loading screen
grammar.colour: fog colour = horizon colour of the sky on both sides; bridge by lerping fog, sun colour and sun elevation, never by a black fade (t02's dark hall is motivated darkness, not a fade)
grammar.signage: labels use the palette already in the assets: cream #f1ede2 on navy #27405a or station green #27512f; signal red #b8432f only for one accent per frame
grammar.people: the engine's people stand where anchors of kind 'boarding', 'seat' and 'poi' are: getting off the train, waiting by the bus door, on the pier, at the lookout. Hospitality is shown by who is waiting, not by text.
grammar.duration: 9–16 s each, skippable after 1.5 s (skip = jump to the last key and hand over)

sound_palette.note: Proposals for WebAudio synthesis in the style of game.js tone(); no audio files exist or are implied. Replace any of them with original or licensed recordings.
sound_palette.bus: one master gain; every loop cue has its own gain node so fades and ducks are ramps (linearRampToValueAtTime), never starts/stops

cues.bike_roll: band-passed noise 700–1100 Hz, gain ∝ speed; plus bike_freewheel
cues.bike_freewheel: clicks (2 ms noise bursts, high-pass 3 kHz) at 14 Hz × speed/5
cues.station_amb: low-passed noise 300 Hz at low gain + sparse footsteps
cues.station_chime: two sine notes 660 → 880 Hz, 0.5 s each, soft attack
cues.train_roll: low-passed noise 220 Hz, gain ∝ speed; double thump (60 Hz sine, 40 ms, twice 90 ms apart) every 25 m of travel
cues.train_brake: band-passed noise sweeping 3 kHz → 1.2 kHz over 1.8 s, Q 12
cues.train_brake_release: white noise, high-pass 2 kHz, 0.35 s decay
cues.door_hiss: white noise, high-pass 2 kHz, 0.5 s, fast attack
cues.footsteps: 30 ms low-passed noise thumps at 1.9 Hz, alternate ±10% pitch
cues.bus_idle: sawtooth 46 Hz through low-pass 220 Hz with 11 Hz tremolo
cues.bus_engine: same voice, 55–95 Hz ∝ speed, low-pass 320 Hz
cues.wind: noise band-pass 400–1200 Hz, centre drifting on a 0.1 Hz LFO
cues.route_tick: 1 ms click through a 2 kHz resonator, very quiet
cues.sea_wash: low-passed noise 500 Hz, gain on a 0.12 Hz LFO (swell), a second layer at 0.31 Hz for the hull slap
cues.ship_engine: sine 38 Hz + 76 Hz, slow 2 Hz throb
cues.ship_horn: two triangle notes 110 + 138 Hz together, 2.2 s, slow attack; (the engine's 'horn' at 311 Hz is the bus/train horn)
cues.harbour_amb: sea_wash at half gain + random metallic ticks (4 kHz, 20 ms) every 1–3 s
cues.apron_amb: noise band-pass 1.8 kHz, very low gain, wide
cues.cabin_chime: two sine notes 880 → 660 Hz, 0.4 s each
cues.jet_idle: noise band-pass 1.6 kHz Q 2 + sine 120 Hz
cues.jet_cruise: noise low-pass 900 Hz + sine 140 Hz; 'pitch_down' = both fall 15%
cues.chile_amb: wind at low gain with a slower LFO; leaf rustle = noise high-pass 3 kHz in 0.4 s swells

sequences.title: The wheel
sequences.idea: The lane ends beside a country halt. The camera comes down to where the bicycle wheel meets the ground; behind it, on the same axis, a steel wheel rests on its rail. The small wheel leaves, the big one starts to turn.
sequences.constraint: The existing train carries its wheels inside the bogie frame: only the lower half of each wheel shows. The match is therefore the contact point (rubber on earth → steel on rail), not a full circle.

set.anchor: end of the Murcia route; track = local z, lane at x = -4.5, platform on +x. World position to be chosen in chapters/murcia.js.

player_stop.note: rear hub lines up with the cab's leading wheel

camera.note: bicycle chase eases low and to the lane side as the rider coasts the last 12 m
rear wheel fills 70% of frame height, hub on the vertical axis, ground line at 30% from the bottom; the bogie and its wheel sit directly behind; rider brakes to a stop
hold: the wheel ticks to rest (freewheel), bell once
push in 3.4 m; the bicycle is wheeled out of frame toward the platform; the steel wheel sits where the rubber one was, rail on the same line as the ground
SPLICE: identical framing on the playable train (camera on the side away from the platform)
the wheel starts to turn; track the hub
pull back and rise into the train's own chase camera; hand over

splice.match: wheel on the vertical axis, contact line 30% from the bottom, wheel diameter ~70% of frame height on both sides
splice.load: preload europe assets from t=0; at 6.0 hold the last rendered frame as an overlay, loadChapter('europe'), place camera on the B key, cross-fade overlay out over 0.6 s

light.bridge: lerp sun colour and fog over the 0.6 s cross-fade; both keys are side-lit close-ups so only the warmth changes

sound.note: gain follows speed down to 0 by 3.4
ticks slowing over 1.2 s
short air hiss on the cut
first rail joint 'clack-clack' lands at 8.0

next.start: route t = 0, train stationary then accelerating; story mode

sequences.reduced_motion: No camera travel: cut from the bicycle chase to key 3.2, 0.4 s cross-fade to the B key at 7.2, then the normal chapter intro. Sounds: bell and one rail clack only.
sequences.no_webgl: Text bridge in the existing fallback list between stages 1 and 2 (i18n key suggested: world.bridge.t01).

sequences.title: Through the station
sequences.idea: The train stops. We get off with everyone else, cross the platform, walk through the station — in by the platform door, out by the street door — and the coach is waiting. One building, two faces, one clock.

set.anchor: europe_v2/station_building. OUT side: stamped at the end of the rail route as in layouts/europe_railway.json. IN side: the same building stamped at the start of the bus route, street face (-z local) toward the road.

bus_start_station_local.note: bus door faces the station; 13 m forecourt

camera.note: inside the coach (seat_view) as the platform slides in; train brakes to 0 by 2.5. Interior view not verified in Blender (the body is closed there) — if the engine cannot see out from seat_view, start on the 3.0 key instead
stopped: the camera slips out through the window line to the platform side; station door and name board under the canopy; doors open (PART_door_*)
walking pace across the platform, head height 1.6 m, slight bob (2 cm)
the doorway fills the frame: natural dark
SPLICE inside the dark of the hall
out of the street door: the coach framed in the opening, door open, people boarding
up the step
seated (passenger_view): the station and its clock in the window as the bus pulls out
hand over to the bus chase camera

splice.match: the station doorway at frame centre; black for 0.5–1.4 s is motivated by the interior
splice.load: preload europe-bus assets from t=0; at 6.2 the screen is the dark hall: loadChapter('europe-bus') here; fade up to key 7.6. If loading runs long, hold the black with station_amb playing.

light.bridge: none needed — keep the europe atmosphere for the first 20 s of the bus chapter, then drift to its own

sound.note: pitch and gain fall with speed
1.8 s squeal ending exactly at standstill (2.5)
4 steps on stone, then 3 on timber floor inside (duller)
low-pass to 600 Hz while indoors, open again at 7.6

next.start: route t = 0 at the station forecourt; story mode

sequences.reduced_motion: Three stills, 0.4 s cross-fades: key 3.0 → key 7.6 → key 12.0. No walk, no head bob.

sequences.title: The horizon
sequences.idea: The road runs to the horizon and the camera lets the bus go, rising until only the line between land and sky is left. A thin route line crosses the frame — a jump in the story, drawn as one. When the picture returns the line is the sea, and the road down the middle of the frame is a ship's deck.
sequences.honesty: This is an ellipsis, not a route: the bus does not drive to Japan. The overlay must say so in its own way (a broken line, a date gap). The sea stage is an aspiration, not a memory — see `stage_tense`.

set.anchor: OUT: the last straight of the bus route (needs >= 300 m of clear view ahead and no backdrop inside +-12 deg of the road axis; use the chapter's own road). IN: open water, the ship at the origin heading +z.

camera.note: bus chase
drift to the road's centre line and stop following: from here the camera is fixed in the world and the bus drives away
crane to 15 m; pitch -2.3 deg puts the horizon at 44% of frame height; road centre line on the vertical axis; bus is a dot
HOLD 3.0 s under the route overlay (see overlay)
SPLICE: same pitch, same horizon height; the keel line replaces the road
hold; the ship's horn answers
descend to the fore deck (deck_spawn + eye height) and hand over

overlay.what: one hairline (2 px, cream #f1ede2, 80% opacity) drawn left to right along the horizon across the full width, broken into dashes over its middle third; two small labels in the game's signage type at its ends. No map, no globe, no country outlines.
overlay.labels: left: the stage just left; right: the stage to come, marked as future. Copy comes from the narrative review (keys suggested: world.bridge.t03.from / .to).

splice.match: horizon at 44% of frame height on both sides; vanishing point at frame centre
splice.load: preload japan assets from t=2; at 5.0 hold the frame as an overlay (the route line animates on top of it) and loadChapter('japan') underneath; reveal with a 0.8 s cross-fade at 8.0

light.bridge: during the hold tint the held frame toward #f1e2d2 (the sea's horizon colour) so the two skies meet at the line

sound.note: with a slow pitch fall (doppler of something leaving)
a soft tick per dash of the route line; nothing melodic
the water arrives before the picture

next.start: at sea on the fore deck or the bridge, whichever the chapter opens on; story mode

sequences.reduced_motion: No crane: cut to key 5.0, show the route line fully drawn (no animation) for 2 s, cross-fade to key 9.2.
sequences.no_webgl: Text bridge between stages 3 and 4 that states the jump and the future tense (world.bridge.t03).

sequences.title: Two lights
sequences.idea: The ship is alongside. From her rail the camera turns away from the quay to the lighthouse and the sea's horizon; the lamp turns, the day goes. When the light comes round again it is a control tower's beacon, the horizon is a runway's, and an aircraft is waiting nose-on.
sequences.honesty: Port and airport are not neighbours: the cut carries a night. Do not show both in one frame.

set.anchor: OUT: layouts/port_departure.json as stamped in the sea chapter, the ship berthed at its layout pose (camera on her fore deck). IN: layouts/asia_arrival.json (aircraft at the layout origin, nose +z).
set.rule: the tower camera stands 170 m from the tower and the deck camera 97 m from the lighthouse — the ratio of the two lamp heights (32.5 / 18.55) — so both towers have the same size on screen; camera heights 9.0 m and 6.1 m put both lamps within 0.6 deg of each other

camera.note: from the bridge as she comes alongside (bridge_view); engines to stop
down to the fore-deck rail on the seaward side, turning away from the quay
ship berthed as in the layout (x = -7, bow +z): lighthouse 12 deg left of axis, lamp 3.3 deg above it, horizon at 63% from the top
HOLD while the light falls to dusk and the lamp sweeps once (flash at 5.6)
SPLICE on the lamp flash: beacon on the same pixel, horizon on the same line; aircraft nose-on at centre
dawn comes up; apron lights go out one by one
crane down from 9 m to the asia_arrival layout camera, then hand over to the chapter

splice.match: lamp/beacon position, horizon height, vertical tower silhouette
splice.load: preload asia assets from t=0; at 5.6 the lamp flash blooms to a warm white overlay (#fff2c8, 0.25 s up) — hold it, loadChapter('asia'), 0.5 s down onto key B. The flash is the loading mask.

light.out: port morning → dusk in 2 s (sun elevation 15° → 2°, sky to #6c7fa6 / horizon #f1b98c)
light.in: asia dawn (same horizon colour, sun returning)
light.bridge: the shared horizon colour #f1b98c on both sides of the flash

sound.note: rigging taps, a mooring creak
one long farewell note, far away
into near silence on the flash
wide, quiet air; a distant APU whine

next.start: aircraft at the stand; story mode. This stage is now the departure toward Chile (order 5).

sequences.reduced_motion: Two stills: key 4.0 and key 8.0, 0.6 s cross-fade, no flash (use a plain fade through #f1b98c).

sequences.title: Through the cloud
sequences.idea: Above a floor of cloud the aircraft sinks until the white takes the frame. It opens on the wall of the Andes in evening light. The camera leaves the aircraft, comes down across the valley to a roadside lookout — and a bicycle is leaning there, the same one. The bell rings once. The rider is home in the world.

set.anchor: OUT: cloudscape relative to the aircraft (end of the flight chapter, any altitude). IN: layouts/chile_arrival.json; the lookout is its origin, the view is +z.

bicycle_at_lookout.note: this is the player's bicycle: the chile chapter (vehicle 'bicycle') starts here, standing still

camera.note: the aircraft's chase anchor, level flight over the cloud floor
ease off the wing; the aircraft starts down (2 m/s) toward the deck
cloud tops rise through frame; white-out complete at 6.0
SPLICE inside the white
the white thins: the snow wall first, then the valley; the aircraft small ahead, continuing its descent out of frame right
one long descending glide across the valley edge to the road behind the lookout — the camera lets the aircraft go
settle behind the bicycle at the parapet: the first image of the game, seen again
hold one second in stillness; bell; hand over to the bicycle chase camera

splice.match: full-frame cloud white (#f4f6f8) on both sides
splice.load: preload chile assets from t=0; the white overlay is the loading mask: loadChapter('chile') at 6.0, thin the overlay over 2 s from 6.6. Scene fog colour = the overlay colour while it thins.

light.bridge: warm the white overlay from #f4f6f8 to #f6e6d2 while it thins, so the Andes are born already in evening light

sound.note: engines back to descent power over 2 s
muffle (low-pass 500 Hz) inside the cloud
the aircraft leaves; do not cut it
dry wind in poplars, far below a dog, nothing else
the same bell as stage 1, once, unanswered

next.start: bicycle standing at the lookout; first input starts the ride. The closing card of the journey belongs to the end of this chapter, not to the transition.
